nodes.name: One-step Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFe-LDH and NiFeZn-LDH were synthesized by one-step hydrothermal method using varied precursor ratios of Zn^{2+} for Ni_{1-x}FeZn_x-LDH (X = 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.20).
nodes.source_text: NiFe-LDH and NiFeZn-LDH were synthesized by one-step hydrothermal method...

nodes.name: Electrochemical Activation
nodes.procedure: The sample NiFeOOH-V_Zn was obtained by a simple electrochemical activation, in which in situ leaching of Zn will promote the reconstruction to form NiFeOOH.
nodes.source_text: ...subsequently, the sample NiFeOOH-V_zn was obtained by a simple electrochemical activation...

nodes.name: Alkaline Etching
nodes.procedure: NiFeZn-LDH was etched under alkaline conditions according to the reported method, the product was named as e-NiFeZn-LDH.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the as-fabricated samples was first characterized by scanning electron microscope (SEM). As shown in Figure S1 (Supporting Information), NiFe-LDH is formed by aggregated irregular nanowires.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH nanosheets have thickness of ≈5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the morphology of NiFeZn-LDH (Figure 2a and Figure S2, Supporting Information) evolves into nanosheets structure with a thickness of ≈5 nm according to the atomic force microscope (AFM) images (Figure S3, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows irregular aggregated nanowires. NiFeZn-LDH presents ultrathin nanosheets. NiFeOOH-V_Zn maintains nanosheets structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further study the structure and morphology of them, the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was applied. As demonstrated in Figure S5a (Supporting Information), the TEM image of NiFeLDH is consistent with the SEM image, presenting an irregular aggregated nanowires.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows lattice fringe of 0.197 nm corresponding to (018) plane. NiFeZn-LDH shows 0.258 nm (012) plane. NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows 0.219 nm (104) plane of NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image (Figure S5b,c, Supporting Information) and fast Fourier transform (FFT) patterns (Figure S5d, Supporting Information) exhibit a lattice fringe of 0.197 nm corresponding to the (018) crystal plane of NiFeLDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Zn, and O. NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows uniform Ni, Fe, O distribution with Zn almost non-existent.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2d shows the high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image and the corresponding elemental mapping images of Ni, Fe, Zn, and O in NiFeZn-LDH sample, demonstrating that these four elements are uniform distribution in the NiFeZn-LDH nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH has Ni:Fe:Zn atomic ratio 10.4:3.8:1. Zn cannot be detected in NiFeOOH-V_Zn.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the atomic ratio of Ni:Fe:Zn is 10.4:3.8:1 (Table S1, Supporting Information) according to the test results of inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-V_Zn SAED pattern verifies formation of NiFeOOH after electrochemical activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the selected area electron diffraction (Figure 2g) also verifies the formation of NiFeOOH after electrochemical activation.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows diffraction peaks at 11.6°, 22.9°, 34.4°, 59.9°, 61.3° for (003), (006), (012), (110), (113) planes. NiFeZn-LDH matches with small angular shift at 11.6° due to Zn doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure and composition of the as-fabricated materials were analyzed via X-ray diffraction (XRD). As demonstrated in Figure 3a, the NiFe-LDH sample shows a series of diffraction peaks at 2θ values of 11.6°, 22.9°, 34.4°, 59.9°, and 61.3°, corresponding to the (003), (006), (012), (110), and (113) crystal face of NiFe-LDH (PDF#40-0215).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows absorption bands at ≈496, 624, 901 cm⁻¹ for M-O, M-O-M, O-M-O. NiFeZn-LDH bands slightly shift confirming Zn doping effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of Zn doped NiFe-LDH was further confirmed by Fourier translation infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, as demonstrated in the Figure 3c, the absorption bands at ≈496, 624, and 901 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the lattice vibrations of M-O, M-O-M, and O-M-O in NiFe-LDH sample, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH: Ni 2p at 855.78, 873.38 eV (Ni²⁺), Fe 2p at 712.08, 724.88 eV (Fe³⁺). NiFeZn-LDH: Ni 2p negative shift 0.38 eV, Fe 2p positive shift. NiFeOOH-VZn: Ni 2p positive shift 0.78 eV indicating higher valence Ni. Zn only in NiFeZn-LDH. O 1s shows M-O, M-OH, H₂O peaks; NiFeOOH-VZn has increased M-O/M-OH ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface chemical valence states and electronic properties of the as-fabricated materials were characterized via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Figure 3d shows the XPS spectra of NiFe-LDH, NiFeZn-LDH and NiFeOOH-V_Zn samples, and Zn was observed only in the NiFeZn-LDH sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-V_Zn has R_ct of 5.60 Ω, lower than NiFe-LDH (10.55 Ω) and RuO₂ (25.80 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was further conducted to evaluate the OER kinetics of the as-fabricated materials. As shown in Figure 4d and Table S3 (Supporting Information), the charge transfer resistances (R_ct) of NiFe-LDH, NiFeOOH-V_Zn, and RuO₂ is 10.55, 5.60, and 25.80 Ω

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-V_Zn double-layer capacitance C_dl = 6.9 mF cm⁻² (higher than NiFe-LDH 1.8 mF cm⁻², RuO₂ 4.8 mF cm⁻²). NiFeZn-LDH shows lower Ni²⁺→Ni³⁺ onset potential (1.42 V vs NiFe-LDH 1.46 V) and larger oxidation peak area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of NiFeOOH-V_Zn sample is 6.9 mF cm⁻², which is much higher than both NiFeLDH (1.8 mF cm⁻²) and RuO₂ (4.8 mF cm⁻²; Figure 4e).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH shows Ni(OH)₂ peaks at 452, 525 cm⁻¹ and FeOOH at 696 cm⁻¹ initially, then NiOOH peaks at 478 (B), 565 (S) cm⁻¹ at lower potential than NiFe-LDH. Higher I_B/I_S ratio indicates γ-NiOOH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy observations combined with electrochemical test demonstrate that in situ leaching of Zn triggers self-reconstruction to from NiFeOOH active centers, and lowers the formation potential of NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows peaks at ≈470, 552 cm⁻¹ (δ(Ni-O), ν(Ni-O) of NiOOH) and ≈690 cm⁻¹ (Fe-O of FeOOH), confirming NiFeOOH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra at ≈470 and 552 cm⁻¹ correspond to the δ (Ni-O) and ν (Ni-O) vibrational modes of NiOOH, and peak at ≈690 cm⁻¹ is ascribed to the Fe-O vibrational mode of FeOOH, as shown in Figure 6c
